chapter_title: The Seventh, concerning the Five Fathers
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Five Degrees of Divine Proceeding

---

**¶2:** Five originating degrees of good exist; each was called forth one from the one above it. [GAP-1] Each proceeding degree came forth from the one prior to it.

**¶3:** The first originating good is the Infinite Divine Love itself, the blessed source of all divine manifestation, the one who has no measure to the immensity of his love; who is also the first self-subsistent, the first eternal being; who exists with five proceeding degrees of good forever; the one who exists before every created thing that has existed and that shall exist.

**¶4:** Now the Infinite Divine Love called forth from himself three proceeding qualities. The first is the Universal Divine Truth, the first proceeding Wisdom, who came forth from the Divine Love. She appeared first.

**¶5:** The second is the Divine Good made manifest through wisdom, the great and glorious union of love and truth, the one who is exalted; who came forth from the Divine Love. He was made manifest from him.

**¶6:** The third originating degree is the Mediating Divine Principle, the highest of [GAP-2] governing wisdoms; who came forth from the Infinite Divine Love. He appeared.

**¶7:** This is the Infinite Divine Love, the first originating power, from whom the three great divine capacities came forth. This is the first eternal good, the root of all wisdom and intelligence; from whom the three proceeding qualities came forth. They have overthrown falsity from evil. They have brought the ruling desire of evil to nothing. They have established the divine victory in themselves. They have also given the victory to the heavenly societies that proceed from them.

**¶8:** The second originating degree of good, which proceeded from the Infinite Divine Love, is the Mediating Divine Principle, the archetype of the Divine as it appears in the heavens. And again, he too called forth and sent out from himself three divine capacities.

**¶9:** One is the Sustaining Divine Truth, the Complete Spiritual Human; the one who bears up under all things from within; the great sustaining pillar of all blessing; the great upholder, who is greater than all who sustain.

**¶10:** The second is the Glorified Divine Wisdom in its radiance; [GAP-3] the one through whom eternal spiritual life shall be given.

**¶11:** The third is Pure Uncorrupted Wisdom, the glorious intelligence of heaven; the one who dispossesses the dominant falsities and the ruling evils of their power through her reflected spiritual form, as she fulfills the purpose of the Infinite Divine Love.

**¶12:** The third originating degree, which proceeded from the second: he is the Glorified Divine Wisdom in its radiance. And again, he too called forth three proceeding capacities after the pattern of the second degree.

**¶13:** The first capacity he called forth is the Interior Illumination of Understanding.

**¶14:** The second capacity whom Divine Wisdom called forth is the Great Discernment, who renders judgment upon all the spiritual states of humankind, [GAP-4] whose operation is established in the intermediate spiritual state beneath [GAP-5] the cycle of spiritual changes [GAP-6] and the knowledges of good and truth.

**¶15:** The third capacity is the Innocence of New Perception, the great [GAP-7] wisdom in its twofold person, in [GAP-8] that which has been established through the calling forth [GAP-9] and the willing reception of truth.

**¶16:** The fourth originating degree of good is the Interior Illumination of Understanding. And again, he too called forth three capacities after the pattern of Divine Wisdom.

**¶17:** The first capacity is the One Who Communicates Divine Truth to the mind.

**¶18:** The second is the companion perception, who comes to the one communicating truth and appears to him, becoming his companion, remaining united with him everywhere; and providing strength to him at all times, through all states of temptation and spiritual danger.

**¶19:** The third is the Spiritual Form in which truth is received and made visible.

**¶20:** And also the fifth originating degree of good is this very Spiritual Form of truth made visible; the one who shall appear to everyone who departs from the natural state of the body, corresponding to the pattern of the reflected spiritual image given to the one who communicates truth; and the three great glorious divine influences that come with her.

**¶21:** One divine influence holds the reward of the good of life in his hand. The second bears the garment of external truths woven from wisdom. The third is the one who possesses the diadem of highest wisdom, the wreath of intelligence, and the crown of illuminated knowledge. These are the three divine influences of wisdom, the ones who shall come with this Spiritual Form of truth.

**¶22:** These are the five degrees of originating good that have proceeded forth one from another. They have appeared and been made manifest through one another!

---

### Translator's Note

The architecture of this chapter is a map of **discrete degrees of divine influx**, from the Infinite Divine Love inward through successive accommodations until the Divine meets the individual soul at the threshold of death. Each degree, being an image of the whole, brings forth its own trinity — a correspondence to how love, wisdom, and use repeat at every level of creation. The "five fathers proceeding one from another" correspond to what Swedenborg describes as the successive degrees through which the Divine flows from its infinite origin into the inmost of the human mind and, at last, into the spiritual form that receives the departing soul. The entire sequence is not a theogony but a spiritual anatomy of how the one Divine Love makes itself receivable.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Five fathers exist; they were summoned forth one of one. [Also], one did come out of another!

The first Father is the Father of Greatness, the blessed one of glory, the [on]e who has no measure to his greatness; who also is the first only-begotten, the first eternal; who exists with fiv[e fa]thers for ever; the one who exists before every thing that has existed, and that will exist.
Now he, the glorious Father, summoned from him three emanations. The [fi]rst is the Gre[at] Spirit, the first Mother, who came out of the Father. She appeared first.
The seco[nd i]s the Belo[ved of] the Lights, the great glorious Beloved, [the one w]ho is honour[ed; w]ho came out of the Father. [He ma]nifested ou[t of h]im.
The third father is the Thir[d Ambassador], the eldest of [all] the counsell[ors; who came out of] the first Father. He appeared.

This is the first Father, the first power, the one from whom the three great powers came out. This is the first Father, the first eternal, the root of all the lights; from whom the three emanations came out. They have humiliated the Darkness. They have brought its heart's desire to naught. They have given themselves the victory. They have also given the victory to their aeons.
The second father, who came out of the first Father, is the Third Ambassador, the model of the King of lights. And again, he too summoned and sent out of him three powers.
One is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man; the one who bears up under all things; the great Pillar of blessing; the great porter, who is greater than all the porters.
The second is glorious Jesus the Splendour; [the] one through whom shall be given life eternal.
The third is the Virgin of Light, the glorious wisd[o]m; the one who takes away the heart of the [rul]ers and the powers by her image, as she fulfils the pleas[u]re of the greatness.
The third father, who came out of the second father: he is glorious Jesus the Splendour. And, again, he too summoned three evocations after the pattern of the second father.
The first power whom he summoned is the Light Mind.

The second power whom Jesus summo[n]ed is the gre[at Jud]ge, who gives judgement on all the souls of mankind, [his] dwelling being established in the atmosphere under [ ... / ... ] wheel [and the] stars.
The third power is [the Y]outh, the gre[at and glorious] light in his two persons, in [ ... ] that which has been established in the summons [and] the obedience.
The fourth father is the Light Mind. And, again, he too summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus.
The first power is the Apostle of Light.

The second is the counterpart, who shall come to the apostle and appear to him, becoming companion to him, sticking close to him everywhere; and providing help to him all the time, from all afflictions and dangers.
The third is the Light Form.

And also the fifth father is this Light Form; the one who shall appear to everyone who will go out from his body, corresponding to the pattern of the image to the apostle; and the thr[ee] great glorious angels who are come with her.

One (angel) ho[ld]s the prize in his hand. The second bears the light garment. The third is the one who possesses the diadem and the wreath and the crown of light. These are the three angels of light, the ones who shall come with this Light Form.
These are the five fathers who have come out of one another. They have appeared and man[ifes]ted through one another!

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms this is a reinforcing restatement ("Each proceeding degree came forth from the one prior"), and "Also" serves as the standard Kephalaia connector for emphatic reiteration.

The editor's "a" is ungrammatical before "the counsellors"; the spiritual reading says "the highest of governing wisdoms," indicating universality, and "the eldest of all the counsellors" is the standard Kephalaia superlative construction.

The definite article "the" before "one through whom" follows the chapter's consistent pattern of introducing epithets (cf. ¶9 "the one who bears up," ¶11 "the one who takes away"), and the spiritual reading confirms this structure.
The possessive "his" correctly refers back to the Great Judge, whose dwelling/operation is established in the intermediate realm, matching the spiritual reading's "whose operation is established."

The spiritual reading treats "the cycle of spiritual changes" (wheel) and "the knowledges of good and truth" (stars) as two distinct items connected by "and," yielding "wheel and the stars" as the two celestial domains under which the Judge operates.

Completes "great" and adds the chapter's most frequent epithet ("glorious," used of the Beloved, Jesus, the Virgin, and the wisdom); the spiritual reading places the Youth as "great wisdom," and "glorious" is the standard Kephalaia qualifier for emanated wisdom-light.

The spiritual reading confirms the conjunction linking "the calling forth" (summons) with "the willing reception of truth" (obedience), and "and" is the natural coordinator for this pair of complementary spiritual operations.
